overview: This passage blocks an easy definitional route to necessity. Modal entailment alone cannot distinguish full from partial grounds, because necessary truths make entailment trivial even when an explanans is incomplete. The argument therefore motivates Trogdon’s later appeal to cognitive significance and essence rather than a purely modal analysis of full grounding.
title: Partial Grounding Distinction
